newsitem.title: BANGLADESH: PRESS DIGEST - Bangladesh Newspapers - June 30.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Bangladesh Newspapers - June 30.

text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Bangladesh press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina leaves early on Tuesday for Tokyo on a six-day official trip to Japan.
Main opposition Bangladesh Nationalist Party has called for countrywide eight-hour general strike on Thursday to protest what it said "anti-people, anti-development and anti-investment budget".
The use of private handling equipment in the Chittagong Port starts from Monday.
U.S. company Occidental will soon bring three rigs to start drilling afresh at the Maulavibazar gas field.
Opposition leader in the parliament Begum Khaleda Zia on Sunday charged the government with failure in revamping the economy and maintaining law and order in the country.

President Justice Shahabuddin Ahmed on Sunday suggested that teachers and studentsd should refrain from party politics on the campus and drastic changes be brought in the country's outmoded education system.
Finance Minister S.A.M.S. Kibria on Sunday withdrew duties on a number of items proposed in the new budget but rejected the plea for withdrawing the much-deabted import surcharge.
Former Finance Minister Saifur Rahman on Sunday warned that the economy would remain sluggish and inflation increase in next few months if economic reforms were not started. REUTER
